text:
sarah: heads up — saw a regression in the nightly perf smoke that looks like starvation of long/large-token sequences when short requests spike. KV hit-rate drops ~30% during the window and the batcher seems to eject long queries.

liam: can you paste the small profiler snippet? curious whether token credits are being grabbed by short lanes too aggressively.

sarah: here's the snippet from the request-level profiler during the 30s window:

```
window_start: 1847654300
batches_formed: 3
avg_tokens_per_batch: 38
kv_evictions_per_s: 82
long_seq_pending: 12 -> 0 processed
batch_ejects_for_long: 7
batcher_wait_ms_p50: 6, p95: 72
```

sarah: TL;DR: short requests form many mini-batches, refill token credits frequently; long lanes starve and end up ejected to keep p50 low. KV cache thrash follows because evictions spike when long KV items are evicted.

priya: hmm — could also be kernel-selection thrashing. For mixed sequence lengths the runtime sometimes picks a conservative fused-kernel path optimized for short seqs which degrades long seq throughput. We saw similar behavior in the quantized branch last quarter.

miguel: agreed. two quick experiments we can try: 1) soft token reservation for long lanes (reserve 20% of token budget), 2) add small early-deadline on mini-batches so long queries wait up to X ms instead of being ejected instantly.

liam: +1 to soft reservation. Another idea: make kernel selection sequence-length-aware before batching decisions — if the queue has >N long seq requests, prefer kernel A that scales better for long runs even if marginally worse for shorts.

sarah: I'll set up an A/B: control = current fair-credit logic, variant A = reserve 20% of per-worker tokens for long-lane (>256 tokens) + min_batch_wait=10ms, variant B = reserve + seq-aware kernel routing.

priya: for profiling, add the following counters so we can correlate: `kv_item_avg_size`, `kv_miss_penalty_ms`, `kernel_choice_per_batch`. Without those we can't prove kernel change is causal.

miguel: config snippet i propose: 

```yaml
batcher:
  min_batch_wait_ms: 10
  token_budget_per_worker: 10000
  reserved_long_tokens_pct: 20
  long_threshold_tokens: 256
kernel_router:
  seq_length_threshold: 256
  prefer_kernel_for_long: fused_gemv_v2
```

liam: small note — prefer_kernel_for_long requires we have a fallback path that preserves latency SLOs for short requests. Also add a quick metric `ejected_long_count` so we can track improvement.

infra-bot: scheduled perf experiments: run `long-reserve-20pct` on canary pool at 1847655400. Results will be posted to #eng-runtime/perf-runs.

sarah: great. I'll run the smoke with KV tracing enabled and attach flamegraphs. If we still see evictions, next step is per-tenant KV caps (limit eviction blast radius).

priya: sounds good. if variant B reduces long latency but increases short p50 >5ms, we need to evaluate overall SLO tradeoff. let's capture p50/p95 across tenant tiers.

miguel: ack — will instrument tiered metrics.

liam: if the experiments are short-lived, also capture kernel selection times so we can rule out extra decision overhead.

sarah: cool — thanks team. will post results in this thread once canary finishes. :rocket:
